# Two Workstation NL witnesses flake on their own instruments

## Context

On #19767 (`4fed2f7c3a`), two Brain-gated e2e shards failed both their attempt and their retry, then passed on re-run (run 38777334496, attempt 3). Sophie's receipt names the jobs (…827, …725); the shards' only code change was a unit fixture. Both failures come from the witness's own instrument, not from a product regression.

## The Problem

**`WorkstationTabDragLabelOverlapNL.spec.mjs:57`.** The positive control "phase A exercised the sort machinery" asserts that a sampled frame shows the designed same-row slide-past crossing (`sameLayer.length > 0`). Locally on `dev` `7f0856c106` the spec failed 2 of 3 runs, always with 0 crossings, never a few. CI showed the same signature: canary 1/17/1, two `DockFlip.play` calls with `geometryOnly: false`. A probe of the same gesture recorded the strip's label order before and after. In 4 of 4 runs the order flipped, from `['Metrics', 'Audit']` to `['Audit', 'Metrics']`; one of those runs sampled 0 crossings and the other three 10. The sort always runs. Whether a sampled frame catches the slide-past overlap is a race, so the control fails on a sort that happened.

**`WorkstationEdgeSplitterNL.spec.mjs:35`.** `findEdgeSplitter` lists the splitters, then calls `getResizeConfig` on each inside `try/catch`. A projection tick can replace a splitter generation between the two calls. The call then hits a destroyed id: the spec catches the throw, but `Neo.ai.Client` logs `Failed to handle message Instance not found: neo-dashboard-dock-splitter-1` (`src/ai/Client.mjs:295`). The `workerErrors` fixture (`test/playwright/fixtures.mjs:136`) fails every test whose page received a worker error the test did not name. So the spec's own probe trips its own oracle, more often on slower runners.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/fixtures.mjs` `workerErrors`: a test names an error it causes with `workerErrors.expect(RegExp)`. Precedent: `DockCrossWindowWitnessNL.spec.mjs:25`, `CanvasGroupPainting.spec.mjs:200`.
- The tab-drag witness's other terminal controls stay as they are: the canary, `DockFlip.play` with `geometryOnly: false`, and the branch classification. The same-row crossings stay recorded as diagnostics, as the spec already labels them.

## The Fix

1. `WorkstationTabDragLabelOverlapNL.spec.mjs`: read the strip's header-label order before and after the gesture, and replace the sampled-crossing control with "the order flipped". Keep the crossings as a logged diagnostic.
2. `WorkstationEdgeSplitterNL.spec.mjs`: take the `workerErrors` fixture, and when a probe of a candidate id throws, name that id's `Instance not found` line, and only that id's.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The tab-drag witness's sort control asserts the order flip, and fails when the gesture does not cross the other label's centre (a mutation shown in the PR).
- [ ] AC-2: The edge-splitter witness names only the `Instance not found` lines of ids its own probe hit; any other worker error still fails it.
- [ ] AC-3: Both specs pass on repeated local runs (`--repeat-each=4 --retries=0`), with the receipt in the PR.

## Out of Scope

Whether the slide-past animation should always paint an overlapping frame, which is cosmetic and not this witness's defect. `Neo.ai.Client` logging failed requests it also returns to the caller is a product contract, left as it is.
